sources.title: Knowledge-Centric Hallucination Detection
aliases: RefChecker: Reference-based Fine-grained Hallucination Checker and Benchmark for Large Language Models

read_scope.not_read: All appendices and released artifact code not audited

findings.claim: Triplet claims are checked using entailment, contradiction and neutral; neutral covers insufficient reference.
Granularity study uses response-level macro-F1; reported 18.2-27.2 point headline refers to correlations in §6.3.

limitations.text: Triplet format can miss complex/temporal semantics; attribution is rudimentary; model prior knowledge can turn neutral into entailment or contradiction.
A triple representation and response-level correlations do not certify v4's natural-language atomic claims or S/C/U reliability; migration not tested.

sources.title: MiniCheck: Efficient Fact-Checking of LLMs on Grounding Documents

read_scope.not_read: All remaining appendix prompts/training details not audited

findings.claim: C2D/D2C target multi-fact, multi-sentence support; contradiction and neutral are merged to unsupported.
Main table uses fixed 0.5 threshold: FT5 average BAcc 74.7, GPT-4 75.3; claim decomposition is not consistently beneficial.

limitations.text: No adequate evaluation of significantly separated or cross-document evidence; English-only training; limited interpretability.
Binary support does not recover C/U; 400x cost comparison is tied to historical models and hardware/API accounting, not a current v4 cost forecast.

sources.title: AlignScore: Evaluating Factual Consistency with A Unified Alignment Function

read_scope.not_read: Full remaining results, limitations and appendices

findings.claim: Model has 3-way, binary and regression heads; final metric uses the 3-way ALIGNED probability.
Final score averages each answer sentence's maximum alignment over roughly 350-token context chunks.

limitations.text: Max-chunk aggregation alone cannot compose evidence located in distinct chunks; sentence averaging targets proportional consistency, unlike any-C/U answer detection. Not an empirical claim about v4 performance.

sources.title: Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models

read_scope.not_read: Rest of results and all appendix demonstrations

findings.claim: Factored verification answers questions without conditioning on the initial draft; the study uses the same LLM, without external tool retrieval.
Closed-book MultiSpanQA Llama65B F1: few-shot .39, joint .46, factored .48.

limitations.text: Generation repair and closed-book factual QA differ from context-only S/C/U; task-specific few-shot demonstrations are not transferable as benchmark-specific v4 inference.
Separate contexts reduce direct copying but do not establish statistically independent errors.

sources.title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet

read_scope.not_read: All appendix prompts and remaining discussion

findings.claim: Intrinsic self-correction excludes external feedback; removing gold-guided stopping changes apparent benefits, and correct-to-incorrect revisions occur.
The paper checks equal-response comparisons and stronger initial instructions.

limitations.text: HotpotQA transition analysis omitted because sample is too small for meaningful statistics.
2023-era models and selected reasoning tasks do not prove impossibility for 2026 models or source-conditioned evidence reviews.

sources.title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems

sections: 4 A New Lens on RAG Performance
read_scope.not_read: All appendices and released source code

findings.claim: Sufficiency asks whether some plausible answer exists from query/context, not whether a fixed candidate answer is entailed.
Autorater accuracy 93% on 115 labeled instances; selection uses confidence plus sufficiency and reports accuracy-coverage, with no added gain in one setting.

limitations.text: Analysis focuses on QA; retrieval-method effects are incompletely explored.
World-correct answers aided by parametric knowledge are not necessarily grounded in supplied context; sufficiency cannot be substituted for S/C/U.

sources.title: FactCG: Enhancing Fact Checkers with Graph-Based Multi-Hop Data

read_scope.not_read: Later limitations and all appendix results/code

findings.claim: CG2C builds multi-premise training pairs via context graphs; CoRe requires both original support and non-support after removal of necessary evidence.
Binary classification uses maximum chunk score; main results tune thresholds per dataset, while unified calibration is left for future work.

limitations.text: Each experiment ran once; about half of evaluated reasoning still categorized as disconnected.
Constructed labels still depend on semantic correctness of LLM graph extraction/editing; tuned-threshold gains do not establish gains under a unified v4 inference policy.

sources.title: Retromorphic Testing with Hierarchical Verification for Hallucination Detection in RAG

read_scope.incidental_scope: Web extraction expanded into first three examples in §4.7; exposure recorded separately
read_scope.not_read: Released toolkit, annotation files and sample files

findings.claim: RT4CHART already combines atomic claims, three labels, answer-span mapping, context evidence and local-to-global verification; global step re-extracts evidence.
Global verification answer-F1 change: +.036 on one dataset and .000 on the other; direct-span ablation removes both decomposition and local checks.

limitations.text: Hedging/certainty shifts, redundant/conflicting context, model dependence, and English RAGTruth-family scope remain limitations.
Related data families limit generality; joint removal of decomposition/local checking cannot identify the local component's causal contribution alone.
